Hi team — confirming the legal/finance position and giving concrete operational guidance you can include in the addendum.

1) Statutory retention windows (high level):
- United States: 7 years (recommended default for tax/audit).
- European Union: varies by member state; safe standard wording is "for the period required by applicable local law (commonly between 6 and 10 years)."
- APAC: varies; include "as required by local law" language and handle exceptions case-by-case.

2) What we must keep vs what we can delete on DSR:
- Must keep: invoices, payment receipts, ledger entries, tax records, and any ledger metadata necessary for audit (invoice numbers, amounts, billing periods, tax IDs). These are accounting records and fall under legal retention obligations; they are not removed by typical erasure requests.
- Can delete/erase: application-level content (messages, model inputs/outputs, user-provided files) subject to standard DSR workflows unless a narrow audit hold applies.

3) Practical approaches to meet both needs:
- Anonymization/pseudonymization: provide a billing extract that retains all financial fields but replaces personal identifiers with hashed IDs. Keep a separate, access-restricted mapping for legal holds only (minimize access and log all access).
- Audit hold process: if a legal/audit hold is necessary, put the account into a hold state preventing erasure of the minimal mapping and accounting records; document the hold period and approval path.
- Data locality: if customer requires ledger residency in a particular jurisdiction, add an explicit SOW line: "Billing ledger replicas will be stored solely in <jurisdiction> for the duration of the contract plus statutory retention period; add-on fees apply."

4) Suggested customer-facing paragraph (short):
"Redwood retains financial and accounting records necessary to comply with applicable law. These records are retained for statutory periods and are not deleted as part of typical Data Subject Erasure requests. Redwood can provide anonymized billing extracts to support customer audits; if physical residency of billing ledgers is required, this can be included as an addendum to the agreement."

5) Next steps for execution:
- Marissa/Rishi: include the short paragraph in the SOW and flag a residency add-on if Quantum confirms.
- Ops/SRE: confirm export format and S3 staging location for the anonymized extracts; include a checklist for redaction.
- Legal: prepare template for notification to customers about audit holds.

I attached the redwood_invoice-retention-summary.pdf we discussed. If Quantum needs exact EU statutory citations, we can run jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction notes but that will add lead time.
